subject: Usage ledger: duplicate attribution between projects causing invoice hold
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@lumina.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lumina Finance <billing@lumina.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@brightwayprocure.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected duplicate attribution on Nov invoice — account on hold

Hi Jordan / team,

We noticed a 47% increase on the Nov 1–11 invoice for our Lumina account and our finance team has placed the payment on hold pending clarification. The surge appears to be coming from requests that should be billed to two separate projects (lumina-core and lumina-research) but are showing up under a single tenant record in your usage ledger.

Quick details:
- Account: Lumina Health (customer id LUM-78)
- Invoice period: 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-11
- Problem window: spikes concentrated 2026-11-03 03:00–07:00 UTC and 2026-11-09 22:00–23:30 UTC
- Impact: unexpected overage ~ $12,400 (we flagged it to our procurement team and put the invoice on hold)

We need the raw evidence for the requests attributed to the wrong project (request_id, timestamp, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, api_key suffix) plus an explanation of how two distinct project labels would collapse into one ledger entry. We're keeping the invoice on hold until the attribution is reconciled — please advise next steps and estimated time to resolution.

Attaching: small sample export (usage-export-20261101-20261111.csv) — we'll follow with a fuller export if helpful.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Operations
Lumina Health

--
Sara P.
Lumina Health | sara@lumina.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@lumina.ai>, Lumina Finance <billing@lumina.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate attribution on Nov invoice — account on hold

Hi Sara — thanks for the heads up and for the sample export. I'm sorry for the disruption; we will prioritize this.

Immediate plan:
1) Ben from Billing/Usage team will ingest the sample and cross‑reference our raw request logs to identify why project tags collapsed.
2) I'll open a temporary collection hold exception on our side until we confirm root cause and agree an adjustment.
3) If this is on us, we'll propose a pro‑rated credit and apply it to the disputed invoice.

Ben — can you take point on matching the request_ids and confirm whether the API key suffixes in Sara's CSV correspond to multiple internal org_ids on our ledger? Please include a snapshot (ledger keys + top 100 offending request_ids).

Sara — can you confirm whether the two projects use separate API keys or a single shared key? That will speed troubleshooting. If you prefer a quick screen share to walk through the CSV, I'm available this afternoon.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Unexpected duplicate attribution on Nov invoice — account on hold

Jordan / Marissa / Logan — initial triage notes (summary):
- Ingested Sara's sample and correlated with our request stream. We see ~3,200 requests in the window that have identical api_key suffixes but are marked with two different project_labels in Lumina's internal metadata. On our ledger these are attributed to a single tenant id (lumina-main) for the affected time slices.
- Hypothesis: an SDK release (lumina internal SDK v4.3.1) changed the header name from X-Project-Tag to X-Redwood-Tag in a way that the proxy strip/normalize path didn't map back to per-project tagging. When header mapping fails, we fall back to the account-level default which is lumina-main.
- Evidence: the ingest-ledger-snapshot-20261111.json (attached) contains contiguous blocks where project_label is null and tenant_id = lumina-main.

Requested next steps from infra: provide 1) per-request raw logs (we can filter to the api_key suffix and timestamps Sara flagged), 2) a short mapping table showing header -> project_label for the 11/03 and 11/09 windows.

Operational ask to Marissa / Logan: anticipate a credit calculation if mapping shows our fallback attribution is responsible. Rough preliminary credit estimate (conservative) is $10,800 — I flagged this in the attached proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx. We'll firm the number once raw logs are cross‑matched.

I'll assemble the top 200 request_ids and pass them to Jordan for sharing.

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst
Redwood Inference
Attachments: ingest-ledger-snapshot-20261111.json, proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@lumina.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@brightwayprocure.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate attribution on Nov invoice — account on hold

Hi Sara — we ran the cross‑match and confirm the attribution collapse is due to header normalization failing for requests from Lumina's v4.3.1 SDK. Ben is right: when the X-Project-Tag header is missing we default to lumina-main (account-level). We're owning the error.

What we propose:
- Hold status: we will not pursue collection on the disputed line items until the reconciliation is complete. Please keep the invoice on hold — we'll mark it as 'under review' in our collection system.
- Credit: we propose to apply a one-time, pro‑rated credit for the misattributed tokens. Attached is a transparent calculation and an example math walkthrough. If Lumina confirms the final list of request_ids, we will issue a credit of the exact amount and reflect it on the next invoice.
- Next steps: Jordan — can you schedule a 30‑minute call this week to review the evidence and sign off on the credit? Carlos — if Lumina's procurement needs a formal credit memo + revised PO instructions, happy to coordinate.

Sara — thank you for the clear sample export; if you can send the full export with the api_key suffix column (or the top 500 request_ids), we will finalize the ledger correction and process the credit within 3 business days.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx
From: Sara Patel <sara@lumina.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@brightwayprocure.com>, Lumina Finance <billing@lumina.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate attribution on Nov invoice — account on hold

Thanks Marissa — that matches what our internal engineering suspected after we rolled v4.3.1 to a subset of jobs. We'll export the top 500 request_ids (including api_key suffix and timestamp) and send them within the hour.

We accept the temporary hold and appreciate Redwood taking ownership. Please confirm the time for the 30‑minute review call — 11/17 at 10:00 AM PT works for our team if that works for you.

Carlos — can you confirm whether Lumina's procurement will need a formal credit memo before we release the PO? Our AP team usually requires a credited invoice before processing payment.

Sara Patel
Head of Platform Operations
Lumina Health
